thread:
maria: Quick sync on cancel semantics at the edge. We need a lightweight way for frontdoor to know whether a client cancel should cause immediate abort, a short drain window, or an ack-with-later-final-status. Current EOF blackholes are causing duplicate side-effects on retries.
ryan: Agreed. Proposal: three behaviors: `abort` (immediate), `drain` (bounded commit window), `ack` (client gets ack, server finishes).
theo: Operational constraint: drain must be bounded per-route+tenant. Add `max_commit_window_ms` and a tenant `drain_budget`. If budget exceeded, downgrade to `abort`.
jess: Observability: tag traces with `cancel_behavior` and emit `edge.cancel.downgraded` and `edge.forced_abort` metrics. Need a way to tell fallback reason: `reason=client_cancel|upstream_error|edge_policy`.
maria: Header sketch: upstream preflight returns `x-rw-supports-retry: yes|no`, `x-rw-max-commit-window-ms: <int>`. Edge exposes `x-rw-cancel-mode` to upstream when opening stream.
ryan: Implementation: do a cheap OPTIONS /_edge_cap preflight per route (cached TTL 5m) so we know retry-safety before streaming tokens.
theo: Enforcement: route schema gains `cancel_mode_default`, `max_commit_window_ms`, `fallback_policy`. Edge enforces hard max and decrements tenant budget on drain.
jess: Failures: if drain timer expires -> force abort and emit `cancel_forced=true` in logs. Also instrument `fallback_attempts` + `duplicate_output_detected` heuristics.
maria: Who owns spikes? @ryan proto preflight headers + small example. @theo add config knobs and quota. @jess metrics + runbook. I'll draft SDK wording about ack vs drain vs abort.
